consensus_summary: Consensus identifies virgin primarily as purity, chastity and exclusive covenant faithfulness to God, most often the Church or Israel as pure virgin bride betrothed to Christ (with Marian virginity and consecrated celibacy as frequent alternatives).
book_summary: Book defines virgin as the espoused—betrothed to one husband with the wedding still ahead: covenant standing, not attainment; law already counts a betrothed virgin a wife; prophets call the re-espoused ten-tribe house “the virgin of Israel”; plural virgins are the bride’s companions; opposite of the harlot.
consensus_core_identification: pure/exclusively faithful bride (Israel or Church) betrothed to God/Christ
book_core_identification: the espoused/betrothed one whose status is covenant standing (wedding still ahead), not attainment
boundary_disagreement: Book narrows virginity to legal/covenantal betrothal status (including post-divorce re-espousal of northern Israel and the bride’s companions) and explicitly excludes “attainment”; consensus admits broader moral-purity, Marian, ascetic-celibacy and readiness cases.
material_contradiction: None; book remains inside the bridal-covenant metaphor and does not deny purity or faithfulness.
rationale: Both cores share the same bridal/espoused referent for God’s people. The book preserves that general category yet materially alters its conditions and precision (standing not attainment; specific re-espousal of the ten-tribe house; companions as virgins) and therefore covers only a subset of the cases consensus admits. This is boundary refinement, not core replacement or novelty.
strongest_objection: A reader could claim the shared betrothal texts make the cores simply equivalent (MATCH) or that “not attainment” quietly contradicts the purity emphasis (DIVERGENT); the explicit redefinition of conditions and the narrowed cases nevertheless favor REFINED.
